topics.title: Review of JSS2 Surahs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recite Surah A'la, Ghashiyah, and Fajr with proper tajwid rules.
The students should be able to explain the main themes of each surah.
The students should be able to identify the number of verses in each surah.

Introduction:
Today we will revise the surahs you learned in JSS2. These surahs are important for your Islamic knowledge and recitation skills.

Content:
Surah A'la (The Most High) is the 87th surah of the Quran with 19 verses. It was revealed in Makkah and emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah. The surah begins with 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' and teaches us about the importance of charity and remembrance of Allah in our daily lives, just like how our parents remind us to pray five times daily.

Surah Ghashiyah (The Overwhelming) is the 88th surah with 26 verses. It contrasts the fate of the righteous and the disbelievers, describing the rewards for the righteous and the punishment for the disbelievers. This reminds us of the importance of good deeds, similar to how a student who studies hard will pass exams while one who plays all day may fail.

Surah Fajr (The Dawn) is the 89th surah with 30 verses. It takes an oath by the dawn and ten nights, then mentions the people of Ad who were destroyed due to their disbelief and arrogance. This teaches us the importance of humility and faith in Allah, just like how a humble person is respected in our community.

Class activity:
Students will be divided into three groups. Each group will select one surah to present to the class. They should recite the surah with proper tajwid, explain its main themes, and discuss one lesson from the surah that applies to our daily lives in Nigeria.

Evaluation questions:
1. How many verses are there in Surah A'la?
2. What is the main theme of Surah Ghashiyah?
3. Which ancient people are mentioned in Surah Fajr?
4. How does Surah Fajr relate to our behavior in school?

Summary:
Today we reviewed three important surahs from JSS2, each teaching us valuable lessons about faith, good deeds, and remembrance of Allah in our lives.

topics.title: Qur'anic Recitation: Suratul Balad (Q90:1- 20) Lessons on moral courage
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recite Suratul Balad verses 1-20 with proper tajwid.
The students should be able to explain the concept of moral courage in Islam.
The students should be able to identify the main lessons from Suratul Balad.

Introduction:
We have learned about several surahs in previous classes. Today we will learn Suratul Balad, which teaches us about moral courage and responsibility.

Content:
Suratul Balad (The City) is the 90th surah of the Quran with 20 verses. It was revealed in Makkah and begins by taking an oath by this city (Makkah) and the surrounding area. The surah emphasizes the difficulty of human existence and Allah's guidance.

Verse 1-2: 'I swear by this city (Makkah) and you are free (from sin) in this city.' This shows the sanctity of Makkah and the special status it holds in Islam.

Verse 3-4: 'And by the begetter and that which he begot.' This refers to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and the people of Quraysh.

Verse 5-10: 'Indeed, man is surely in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise each other to truth, and advise each other to patience.' This verse highlights the importance of faith, good deeds, and encouraging others to do good.

The surah teaches us about moral courage - standing up for what is right even when it's difficult. In Nigeria, this could mean speaking out against corruption or helping a neighbor in need despite personal challenges.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create a short role-play demonstrating moral courage in everyday Nigerian situations, such as refusing to cheat in exams or standing up for a classmate being bullied. They should perform their role-play for the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Suratul Balad begin with?
2. According to verse 5, who is in loss?
3. What three things save a person from loss according to the surah?
4. How can you show moral courage in your school?

Summary:
Suratul Balad teaches us about human challenges and the importance of faith, good deeds, and patience in overcoming life's difficulties with moral courage.

topics.title: Qur'anic Recitation: Suratul Shams (Q91:1- 15) Lessons on purity and righteousness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recite Suratul Shams verses 1-15 with proper tajwid.
The students should be able to explain the lessons on purity and righteousness from the surah.
The students should be able to differentiate between physical and spiritual purity.

Introduction:
After learning about moral courage in Suratul Balad, today we will study Suratul Shams, which teaches us about purity and righteousness.

Content:
Suratul Shams (The Sun) is the 91st surah of the Quran with 15 verses. It was revealed in Makkah and takes oaths by various natural phenomena to emphasize Allah's power and the importance of human responsibility.

Verse 1: 'By the sun and its brightness.' This reminds us of Allah's creation and the beauty of nature around us in Nigeria, from the harmattan season to the rainy season.

Verse 2-4: 'And by the moon when it follows it. And by the day when it displays it. And by the night when it covers it.' These verses highlight the perfect order in creation.

Verse 5-6: 'And by the soul and He who proportioned it. And inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.' This shows Allah's power over the human soul and the capacity for both good and evil within us.

Verse 7-8: 'He has succeeded who purifies it. And he has failed who instills it with corruption.' This is a powerful lesson about the importance of spiritual purification and righteousness.

The surah teaches us that just as we keep our bodies clean in our hot Nigerian climate, we must also keep our souls pure through good deeds, prayer, and avoiding sinful acts. Righteousness means doing what is pleasing to Allah in all aspects of life.

Class activity:
Students will write a short paragraph explaining how they can maintain both physical and spiritual purity in their daily lives, using examples from Nigerian culture and environment. They will share their paragraphs with a partner.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Suratul Shams begin with?
2. What is inspired in the human soul according to verse 6?
3. What happens to those who purify their souls?
4. How can purity be applied to our behavior in the marketplace?

Summary:
Suratul Shams teaches us about the importance of spiritual purity and righteousness, reminding us that success comes from purifying our souls and instilling goodness within ourselves.

topics.title: Qur'anic Recitation: Suratul Layl (Q92:1-21)
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to memorize Suratul Layl verses 1-21.
The students should be able to explain the rewards of good deeds according to the surah.
The students should be able to identify how the surah contrasts the righteous and the disbelievers.

Introduction:
We have studied several surahs that teach us about moral values. Today we will learn Suratul Layl, which focuses on the rewards of good deeds and the contrast between the righteous and the disbelievers.

Content:
Suratul Layl (The Night) is the 92nd surah of the Quran with 21 verses. It was revealed in Makkah and takes oaths by night and day to emphasize Allah's power and the importance of human effort.

Verse 1-2: 'By the night when it covers. And by the day when it appears.' These verses highlight the natural order that Allah has established.

Verse 3-5: 'Indeed, there is for man a success that will attain it. And whatever he strives for is but for the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to your Lord is the return.' This teaches us that true success comes from striving for Allah's pleasure, not just worldly gains.

Verse 6-7: 'And He is the one who made you successive generations in the earth. And you will be raised after death.' This reminds us of the afterlife and accountability.

Verse 8-14: 'So when the deafening blast occurs. And the Day of Resurrection occurs. And the Hellfire is brought forth on that day. And the Paradise is brought forth on that day. The man will know what he has sent forth and left behind.' These verses describe the Day of Judgment and its consequences.

Verse 15-21: 'Indeed, man is indeed a transgressor. Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin each other with truth and enjoin each other with patience.' This contrasts the transgressing humanity with those who believe, do good deeds, and encourage others to truth and patience.

The surah teaches us that good deeds have eternal rewards, while worldly pleasures are temporary. In Nigeria, this could mean helping a neighbor with their farm work, sharing food with the less fortunate, or studying hard to gain knowledge that benefits others.

Class activity:
Students will create a chart comparing the characteristics and fate of the righteous and the disbelievers as described in Suratul Layl. They will include examples from Nigerian life for each category.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Suratul Layl begin with?
2. What is the main difference between the righteous and the disbelievers according to the surah?
3. What happens on the Day of Resurrection according to verses 11-14?
4. How can we apply the lesson of patience in our Nigerian society?

Summary:
Suratul Layl teaches us about the importance of good deeds and patience, contrasting the eternal rewards for the righteous with the temporary nature of worldly pleasures.

topics.title: MID-TERM EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their knowledge of the surahs studied this term.
The students should be able to apply tajwid rules in recitation.
The students should be able to explain the main lessons from the surahs.

Introduction:
Today is your mid-term examination. This test will assess your understanding of the surahs and tajwid rules we have studied this term.

Content:
The examination will cover the following topics:
1. Review of JSS2 Surahs (A'la, Ghashiyah, Fajr)
2. Suratul Balad (Q90:1-20) - moral courage
3. Suratul Shams (Q91:1-15) - purity and righteousness
4. Suratul Layl (Q92:1-21) - rewards of good deeds

The examination will include:
- Recitation of selected verses from each surah with proper tajwid
- Multiple choice questions on the main themes of each surah
- Short answer questions explaining the lessons from each surah
- Application questions connecting the surahs to everyday Nigerian life

Remember to read each question carefully before answering. Manage your time well during the examination.

Class activity:
Students will complete the mid-term examination paper. The teacher will distribute the examination papers and provide instructions. Students will work individually and silently for the duration of the examination period.

Evaluation questions:
The mid-term examination will serve as the evaluation for this week. Questions will assess students' knowledge of the surahs studied, their ability to recite with proper tajwid, and their understanding of the main lessons from each surah.

Summary:
The mid-term examination has tested your knowledge and understanding of the surahs and tajwid rules we have studied this term. Your results will help identify areas for improvement before continuing with the remaining topics.

topics.title: Rules of Ghunnah (Nasal Sound)
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify the letters that require ghunnah.
The students should be able to apply ghunnah rules during recitation.
The students should be able to differentiate between ghunnah and other tajwid rules.

Introduction:
After our mid-term break, we will now learn about an important aspect of tajwid - the rules of ghunnah or nasal sound. This will improve your Quranic recitation.

Content:
Ghunnah is a nasal sound produced when certain letters are pronounced. It is an essential aspect of tajwid that affects the beauty and accuracy of Quranic recitation.

Letters that require ghunnah:
1. Meem (م) - when it has a shaddah or sukoon
2. Noon (ن) - when it has a shaddah or sukoon
3. Tanween (double vowel) - which produces an 'n' sound

Ghunnah characteristics:
- Duration: Ghunnah should last for two counts (approximately 1-2 seconds)
- Quality: It should be a clear nasal sound without vibration in the throat
- Application: It occurs when the nasal passage is blocked and air is released through the nose

Examples of ghunnah in the Quran:
- In Surah Al-Fatiha: 'Ar-Rahman Ar-Raheem' (الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ) - the noon in 'Raheem' has ghunnah when stopping
- In Surah Al-Ikhlas: 'Allah Ahad' (ٱللَّهُ ٱلأَحَدُ) - the meem in 'Ahad' has ghunnah when stopping
- In Surah Al-Falaq: 'Min kulli shayyin yadheeh' (مِّن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يَضُرُّ) - the meem has ghunnah

Common mistakes in ghunnah:
- Making ghunnah too short or too long
- Not producing ghunnah when required
- Confusing ghunnah with idgham (merging letters)

In Nigerian context, think of ghunnah like the sound made when saying 'mmhmm' in agreement, but longer and more controlled. Just as we emphasize certain words when speaking to our elders, ghunnah emphasizes certain letters in Quranic recitation.

Class activity:
Students will practice reciting verses containing ghunnah letters. They will work in pairs, taking turns to recite and provide feedback on each other's application of ghunnah rules. The teacher will circulate to provide guidance and corrections.

Evaluation questions:
1. Which two letters require ghunnah when they have shaddah or sukoon?
2. How long should ghunnah last during recitation?
3. Give an example of a word in the Quran that contains ghunnah.
4. What is the difference between ghunnah and idgham?
5. Why is ghunnah important in Quranic recitation?

Summary:
Ghunnah is an essential tajwid rule that produces a nasal sound when specific letters are recited. Proper application of ghunnah rules enhances the beauty and accuracy of Quranic recitation.

topics.title: MID-TERM BREAK
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and recharge for the continuation of the term.
The students should be able to reflect on their learning so far.
The students should be able to prepare for the topics to come after the break.

Introduction:
This week is our mid-term break. It is important to rest and reflect on what we have learned so far in Islamic Studies this term.

Content:
The mid-term break is a time for:
1. Rest and relaxation: After weeks of hard work, it is important to rest your body and mind. Just as our farmers rest after the planting season, students need rest to perform well.
2. Reflection: Think about what you have learned about the surahs and tajwid rules. Consider which topics you found easy and which ones were challenging.
3. Revision: You may want to revise the surahs we have studied - A'la, Ghashiyah, Fajr, Balad, Shams, and Layl. Practice reciting them with proper tajwid.
4. Preparation: Think about the topics we will cover after the break, such as more tajwid rules and new surahs.

During this break, you should also continue your daily prayers and Quranic recitation. Maintaining your connection with Allah during the break will help you return refreshed and ready to learn.

Class activity:
During the break, students are encouraged to:
1. Spend quality time with family and friends
2. Visit the mosque for additional prayers
3. Read the Quran daily, focusing on proper pronunciation
4. Keep a journal of their reflections on what they have learned
5. Help with household chores, as serving others is an act of worship in Islam

Evaluation questions:
The mid-term break does not have formal evaluation questions. However, students should be prepared to discuss their experiences and reflections when they return to class after the break.

Summary:
The mid-term break is an important time for rest, reflection, and spiritual rejuvenation. Use this time wisely to strengthen your connection with Allah and prepare for the continuation of your Islamic Studies.

topics.title: Rules of Waqf (Stopping Signs)
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify the different waqf signs in the Qur'an, explain the importance of proper stopping during recitation, and demonstrate correct application of waqf rules in selected verses.

Introduction:
We have learned how to recite the Qur'an with proper pronunciation through tajwid rules. Today, we will learn about the stopping signs in the Qur'an, which help us understand the meaning better.

Content:
Waqf means stopping or pausing in recitation. There are different types of waqf signs in the Qur'an:

1. Complete stop (Taam): This sign is represented by a circle ○ over the word. It indicates that recitation should stop completely at this point.
2. Permissible stop (Jaiz): This sign is represented by a comma-like symbol. It means stopping here is allowed but not necessary.
3. Recommended stop (Mustahab): This sign is represented by a square. It is recommended to stop here for better understanding.
4. Prohibited stop (Munakahat): This sign is represented by a semicolon. Stopping here changes the meaning and should be avoided.

For example, in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 201, there is a complete stop sign after the word 'muslimoon', indicating a complete pause before continuing with the next verse.

In Nigerian markets, when a trader is explaining prices, they pause at important points to ensure customers understand. Similarly, waqf signs help us understand the message of the Qur'an better.

Class activity:
Divide the class into groups. Give each group a verse from the Qur'an with waqf signs. Students should practice reciting the verse with proper stopping at the indicated signs.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does waqf mean?
2. List two types of waqf signs and explain their meanings.
3. Why is proper stopping important in Qur'anic recitation?
4. What is the difference between a complete stop and a permissible stop?

Summary:
Understanding waqf signs is essential for proper recitation and comprehension of the Qur'an's message.

topics.title: Practical Tajwid Exercises
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recite selected verses with correct tajwid rules, identify and correct common tajwid mistakes in recitation, and participate effectively in group recitation activities.

Introduction:
We have studied various tajwid rules throughout the term. Today, we will practice applying these rules in our recitation to improve our pronunciation and understanding.

Content:
Tajwid means making beautiful or excellent recitation. It involves proper pronunciation of Arabic letters and applying rules to the Qur'an. Let's practice some common tajwid rules:

1. Madd (elongation): When certain letters follow a madd letter, the sound is elongated. For example, in Surah Al-Fatiha, the word 'ar-rahman' has a madd that is elongated for two counts.
2. Ghunnah: This is a nasal sound produced when pronouncing letters like meem and noon with shaddah. For example, in the word 'min' in Surah Al-Fatiha.
3. Ikhfa: This is a partial concealment of the letter when it has a sukoon and is followed by a non-corresponding letter. For example, in the word 'min rabbika' in Surah Al-Fatiha.
4. Idgham: This is the merging of one letter into another. For example, when the noon with sukoon is followed by meem, it is merged into the meem sound.

In our local masjids during Ramadan, we hear beautiful recitation with proper tajwid. This practice helps us understand the Qur'an better and increases our connection with Allah.

Class activity:
Divide the class into small groups. Each group will select a short surah or portion of a surah to recite. They will take turns reciting while others listen and provide constructive feedback on tajwid application.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does tajwid mean?
2. Explain one madd rule with an example from the Qur'an.
3. What is ghunnah and when does it occur?
4. Why is practicing tajwid important for Qur'anic recitation?

Summary:
Regular practice of tajwid rules improves our recitation and deepens our connection with the Qur'an.

topics.title: Importance of the Qur'an in Muslim Life
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of the Qur'an in daily life, identify how the Qur'an provides guidance, and describe ways the Qur'an serves as a source of healing and reflection.

Introduction:
We have studied the rules of reciting the Qur'an properly. Now, let's explore why the Qur'an is so important in the life of a Muslim and how it guides us in our daily activities.

Content:
The Qur'an is the holy book of Islam revealed to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W). It plays several important roles in a Muslim's life:

1. Guidance: The Qur'an provides guidance for all aspects of life. For example, Surah Al-Baqarah verse 2 says: "This is the Book, in it is guidance sure, without doubt, to those who fear Allah." Just as a compass guides travelers in the desert, the Qur'an guides Muslims through life's journey.

2. Healing: The Qur'an is a source of spiritual healing. Surah Al-Isra verse 82 says: "And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers." When we feel worried or sad, reciting the Qur'an can bring peace to our hearts.

3. Reflection: The Qur'an encourages us to reflect on Allah's creation. Surah Al-Imran verse 190-191 says: "Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth... there are signs for men of understanding." When we look at the harmattan season and see how it changes our environment, we can reflect on Allah's power.

4. Daily reference: Muslims use the Qur'an for daily decisions, from what to eat (halal food) to how to interact with others. Just as a market trader follows certain rules in business, Muslims follow the guidance of the Qur'an in all aspects of life.

Class activity:
Students will write down a personal challenge they are facing and find a verse from the Qur'an that provides guidance for that situation. They will share their findings with the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. How does the Qur'an provide guidance in a Muslim's life?
2. What does the Qur'an say about being a source of healing?
3. Give an example of how you can reflect on Allah's creation using the Qur'an.
4. Why is the Qur'an important for daily decision making?

Summary:
The Qur'an is a complete guide for Muslims, providing spiritual healing, wisdom, and direction for all aspects of life.

topics.title: REVISION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall and explain tajwid rules studied this term, recite selected surahs with proper tajwid and waqf, and demonstrate understanding of the importance of the Qur'an in Muslim life.

Introduction:
This week, we will revise all the topics we have covered this term to prepare for our end-of-term examination. Let's review the key concepts and rules we have learned.

Content:
We will revise the following topics:

1. Tajwid rules: We have studied various rules including madd, ghunnah, ikhfa, and idgham. These rules help us recite the Qur'an beautifully and correctly.

2. Waqf signs: We learned about different stopping signs in the Qur'an including complete stop, permissible stop, recommended stop, and prohibited stop. These signs help us understand the meaning better.

3. Importance of the Qur'an: We discussed how the Qur'an provides guidance, healing, and encourages reflection. It is a complete guide for Muslims in all aspects of life.

4. Surahs studied: We have recited and studied various surahs including Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, and Al-Imran. Each surah contains important lessons for Muslims.

In our local communities, elders often remind us of important lessons before special occasions. Similarly, this revision helps us remember the important lessons we have learned about the Qur'an and its recitation.

Class activity:
Divide the class into teams. Each team will be given a tajwid rule or waqf sign to explain and demonstrate. They will also be asked to recite a verse that applies the rule or sign they were given.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the difference between ikhfa and idgham with examples.
2. Why is the Qur'an described as a source of healing?
3. What are the four types of waqf signs we studied?
4. How does the Qur'an provide guidance in daily life?

Summary:
Revision helps us strengthen our understanding of the Qur'an and its recitation, preparing us for the examination and for applying these lessons in our daily lives.

topics.title: EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of tajwid rules, waqf signs, and the importance of the Qur'an in Muslim life through written examination.

Introduction:
Today, you will take your end-of-term examination in Islamic Studies. This examination will test your understanding of the topics we have covered this term, particularly tajwid rules, waqf signs, and the importance of the Qur'an.

Content:
The examination will cover the following areas:

1. Tajwid rules: Questions will test your knowledge of various tajwid rules including madd, ghunnah, ikhfa, and idgham. You may be asked to identify these rules in given verses or explain their application.

2. Waqf signs: Questions will assess your understanding of different waqf signs and their proper application in recitation. You may be asked to identify waqf signs in given verses or explain their meanings.

3. Importance of the Qur'an: Questions will test your understanding of how the Qur'an provides guidance, healing, and encourages reflection. You may be asked to explain specific verses that demonstrate these aspects.

4. Surahs studied: Questions will assess your knowledge of the surahs we have recited and studied this term, including their key themes and lessons.

Just as students in other subjects prepare for examinations by reviewing their notes, you have been preparing for this examination by studying and practicing tajwid rules and understanding the importance of the Qur'an.

Class activity:
The examination will be conducted in a quiet examination hall. Students will work individually to complete the examination paper within the allocated time.

Evaluation questions:
The examination will contain multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions covering all topics studied this term.

Summary:
The examination is an opportunity to demonstrate your knowledge and understanding of Islamic Studies, particularly the recitation and understanding of the Qur'an.

topics.title: CLOSING/VACATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning this term, identify areas for improvement in their Qur'anic recitation, and set goals for continued study during the vacation period.

Introduction:
As we conclude this term, let's reflect on what we have learned about the Qur'an and its recitation, and how we can continue to improve during the vacation.

Content:
This term, we have studied several important topics:

1. We learned about tajwid rules that help us recite the Qur'an beautifully and correctly.
2. We studied waqf signs that help us understand the meaning of the Qur'an better through proper stopping.
3. We explored the importance of the Qur'an in providing guidance, healing, and encouraging reflection in our daily lives.
4. We practiced reciting various surahs with proper tajwid and understanding.

During the vacation, you can continue to improve your recitation by:
- Setting aside time each day for Qur'anic recitation
- Reviewing tajwid rules
- Listening to renowned reciters
- Attending Islamic programs in your local community
- Teaching younger family members what you have learned

In Nigerian families, elders often encourage children to use vacation time for religious learning. Similarly, you can use this time to strengthen your connection with the Qur'an.

Class activity:
Students will write down three personal goals for improving their Qur'anic recitation and understanding during the vacation. They will share one goal with the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is one important thing you learned this term about the Qur'an?
2. How will you continue to improve your recitation during the vacation?
3. Why is it important to maintain regular Qur'anic study even during vacation?

Summary:
As we end this term, remember that learning about the Qur'an is a lifelong journey. Use the vacation time to strengthen your connection with the Qur'an and prepare for continued learning next term.
